reason: Verified in code and by driving. grep for data-act="retry" returns exactly three hits repo-wide: render-b.js:1545 (the draw site), the generated console.html copy of it, and interaction-check.mjs:2198 which only counts it. states["loading-slow"] registers no listener at all, and no delegated [data-act] handler in render-b.js or render-core.js reaches it. Driven at 390x844 on ?v=approach&state=loading-slow: pressing the button (pointer, and Enter on the focused button) changes nothing but document.activeElement — .tl-stage innerHTML byte-identical, body text identical, .b-field aria-busy stays "false", the four .b-skel bars unchanged, still identical 3.2s later, no console errors. There is no .b-live anywhere in this state, so there is not even a silent announcement (the finding's phrasing 'stays empty' understates it). It is the single focusable element in the state (ended has zero), so it is the audience's only offered move at the one moment the product is failing them. This is not taste: render-b.js:470-471 states the lab's own rule directly above the helper that enforces it - 'Anything not built is inert text, never a focusable promise' - and inert() is used exactly that way one screen over, beside a fully wired Copy the link that sets its button label, writes .b-live and has a failure path (render-b.js:1375-1399). Try again is the one control in the master that breaks the rule the master wrote. The gate does not cover it and is not restated by this: 'and offers a way on' asserts slow.way === 1, i.e. the button exists; the 'every control does something' loop at interaction-check.mjs:1123-1147 iterates only owner-flight, owner-empty, owner-editing, publish, phone, desk, day, and its sameness test includes document.activeElement.className, so a press that only moves focus would register as alive even if loading-slow were added. Both halves of the finding's diagnosis of the gate check out. No constraint is touched: the fix is behaviour, no new hue, weight or structure.
sharpenedFix: Wire retry in the guest branch on the copy pattern already in the file. On press: set .b-field aria-busy="true", restore the loading face (the four .b-skel bars and 'Bringing in what is ahead.'), keep focus on the button, and announce through a .b-live status node - which must be ADDED, since loading-slow currently has none. After the stall interval, restore the stalled face and put 'Still not arriving. The plan has not been deleted, and the link still works.' into .b-live so a screen reader hears the second failure rather than nothing. Do not let the button label be the only signal. Two corrections to the proposed gate change: (a) adding 'ended' to the every-control-does-something loop is a no-op - ended has zero focusable elements, so dead.length === 0 trivially; if the panel wants ended guarded, it needs its own assertion that a dead-end state offers a named next step, not this loop; (b) the load-bearing edits are adding 'loading-slow' to the state list AND dropping active from the before/after sameness comparison at interaction-check.mjs:1132/1140, since focus alone must not count as the control having acted. Additionally assert directly that pressing [data-act="retry"] flips .b-field aria-busy to true and writes non-empty text into .b-live, so a future silent regression cannot pass by moving focus.
